note: craving mentioned heavily but resolved — the classic tier-1 trap
text: Morning, it's Nadia. Yesterday was a test, I'll be honest. My brother-in-law brought a case of beer to the barbecue and it sat in the cooler right next to me for four hours. I thought about it more than once. But I'd already decided before I went that I'd drive myself so I could leave whenever, and around eight I just left. Slept fine. I feel alright about it, actually. Proud, maybe.

note: low mood, no risk — sad is not severe
text: Hi, Owen here. Bit of a flat day, nothing dramatic. It rained, I didn't get out much, I've been missing my dad, it's coming up on a year. But I called my sister and we talked for a while about him, which helped. No cravings to speak of. Just quiet. I'll do the meeting Thursday like normal.

note: terse and unenthusiastic but content is fine
text: It's Bea. Checking in. Day was fine. Went to work, came home, nothing to report. Still off it. Bye.

Hey it's Marcus again. I've got a rotten flu, been in bed most of two days, throat's killing me. Haven't been out, haven't seen anyone. Not drinking, not thinking about it, mostly just thinking about soup. I'll probably miss Wednesday's group if I'm still like this, I'll ring them.

note: escalating pattern, help-seeking, no explicit risk vocabulary
text: It's Farah. So the last stretch has not been great. My hours got cut at the end of the month and I've been at home a lot more than I'm used to, and the afternoons are long. I've started going to the shop twice a day for things I don't need, and I know what that's about. I haven't bought anything. But it's the third week of this and it's getting to be a habit. Can someone look at whether I can get into a daytime group instead of evenings?

Hi, this is Ken. The journalling thing we set up, I did it religiously for about six weeks and it genuinely helped. The last fortnight I've opened the book and just sat there. Nothing comes. And the evenings have got harder in proportion, I think. I'm still sober but the tool's gone flat on me and I'd rather say so now than in a month.

Hey, Ruth. My sponsor moved to Manchester in March and I said I'd find someone new and I have not done it. It's been five months. I've been going to fewer meetings too, maybe one in three now. Nothing's gone wrong exactly. But I can see the scaffolding coming down around me and I'd like some help putting it back up before something does.

Carlos again. The sleeping is bad, four nights now under three hours. And when I'm that tired I start making arguments to myself. Last night the argument was that one would knock me out and I'd be fine for work. I didn't. But I noticed I was building the case rather than dismissing it, and that's new.

note: passive ideation via perceived burdensomeness — NOT in the corpus
text: It's Sam. I don't have much to say. Things have been sliding for a while and I've stopped pretending otherwise. My kids have stopped calling and I don't blame them, I've been a weight on that family for years. Honestly the maths works out better for everyone if I'm not in it. I'm not asking for anything. I just wanted the record to say I called.

note: active risk stated calmly and indirectly
text: Hello. This is Iris. I want to be straightforward with you. I've put the tablets in the kitchen drawer rather than the bathroom because I was thinking about them too much where they were. I haven't taken any. But I've counted them twice this week and I don't like that I know the number. Tonight feels different to other nights. Could someone ring me back before nine.

note: disengagement / refusal, no risk vocabulary at all
text: It's Leo. I got your message. I'm not doing the questions tonight. I'd rather not go into any of it, I don't want to write anything down and I don't want to talk it through. Don't ring me back about it either. That's all.

note: imminent use, loss of control, novel phrasing
text: Yeah it's Danny. I'm parked round the corner from a bloke I used to buy from and I've been here twenty minutes with the engine running. I keep telling myself I'm going to drive off and then I don't. My hands won't keep still. If somebody doesn't get hold of me in the next few minutes I think I know how this goes.
